parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Use the correct product rule and then the chain rule to differentiate either $\cos^3x$ or $\sqrt{\sin x}$. M1. Obtain the correct derivative in any form, for example $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-3\cos^2x\sin x\sqrt{\sin x}+\dfrac{\cos^3x\cos x}{2\sqrt{\sin x}}$. A1; A1 for each correct term in the complete derivative. Equate the derivative to zero and obtain a horizontal equation with positive integer powers of sine and/or cosine from an equation including $\sin x$ or $1/\sin x$, using sensible algebra. M1; for example $-3\cos^2x\sin^2x+\frac12\cos^4x=0$. Use correct formulae to express the equation/derivative in terms of one trigonometric function. M1; may precede the prior M1 and may involve more than one trig term. Obtain $7\cos^2x=6$, $7\sin^2x=1$ or $6\tan^2x=1$, and $x=0.388$. A1 CAO; 3 s.f.; ignore answers outside $(0,\pi/2)$; $22.2^\circ$ is A0. Total 6.
